headline: High Desert Camping and Summit Permits
reservation: A wilderness permit is required year-round for overnight wilderness camping. Reserve available sites through Recreation.gov, then obtain the permit in person at Pine Springs Visitor Center before departure. Walk-up permits for unreserved sites may be issued there from 8 AM to noon, up to 24 hours in advance. Front-country campground reservations are separate.

days.title: The Top of Texas

stops.name: Guadalupe Peak Trail
stops.detail: Climb the highest point in the state to view the vast salt flats and Chihuahuan Desert from the summit.

stops.name: Frijole Ranch Cultural Museum
stops.detail: Visit this historic ranch house to learn about the region's human history and see the nearby spring-fed oasis.

days.driving: Minimal; walking/hiking from central trailhead area
days.note: High winds are frequent; check the mountain forecast before attempting the summit.

days.title: Canyons and Fall Colors

stops.name: McKittrick Canyon Trail
stops.detail: Walk among maple and ash trees that display vibrant colors during the autumn months.

stops.name: Pratt Cabin
stops.detail: A stone structure serving as a mid-point destination within the canyon's lush riparian zone.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from Pine Springs to McKittrick entrance
days.note: McKittrick Canyon day-use area has specific gate hours; check current seasonal closing times.

days.title: Desert Floor and Dunes

stops.name: Salt Basin Dunes
stops.detail: Explore the stark white gypsum dunes on the park's western edge for a distinct geological perspective.

stops.name: Smith Spring
stops.detail: A shorter loop trail leading to a desert spring that supports local wildlife and lush vegetation.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the round trip to the Dunes; roads vary
days.note: The road to the dunes is unpaved and can become impassable after heavy rain.

intel.title: McKittrick Congestion
intel.text: The McKittrick Canyon lot often fills by mid-morning during peak November foliage. Arrive early or consider visiting the less-crowded Frijole Ranch area instead.

intel.title: Remote Communication
intel.text: Expect no cellular service throughout most of the park and surrounding desert. Carry a satellite messenger for emergencies in the backcountry.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: There are no gas stations within the park. Refill in Carlsbad or El Paso before approaching the Pine Springs visitor center.

intel.title: Summer Heat Safety
intel.text: Midday temperatures regularly exceed 100 degrees in summer. Plan strenuous hiking for dawn and seek shade by noon to avoid heat exhaustion.

intel.title: Salt Basin Access
intel.text: The Salt Basin Dunes are accessed via a different entrance near Dell City, not the main Pine Springs area. Allow significant travel time between these two regions.

plan.arrival: Collect supplies and water in El Paso or Carlsbad; the park provides no groceries. Check-in at the Pine Springs Visitor Center for orientation.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is fine for the main visitor area, but high-clearance is necessary for the road to Dog Canyon or Salt Basin. Check rental rules for unpaved roads.
plan.goldenHour: The western face of El Capitan is best viewed from the Salt Basin Dunes at sunset, depending on seasonal cloud cover.
